title: Lips Page, Basie and the Blue Devils; Claude Kennedy
summary: Albert says he played with Lips Page when Moten's Blue Devils came to Dallas in 1926. He recalls Claude Kennedy, whose place he took in Troy Floyd's band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well now you're talking about blues and Judy Williams and all that. Did you know Lips Fades when you were in fact?

Lips and I played together. Lips came to Dallas, Texas in 1926 with Benny Moulton's Blue Devils. And Basie was the pianist in this band. And Oren Page was the bass. So they thought that Lips Page and Oren and the Brothers weren't even related. And Page and I, we used to go out at night and sit out and play with each other. And Compton with John on the piano.
Well what about his style then? Beautiful. Great style. Did he sound the same as he did on the record with, say, LATER in 32?

I think he sounded better. I think he sounded better in person. One man that they weren't able to capture, I don't think, I've never heard anything from him, was Claude Benno Kennedy. I took his place in Troy Floyd's band. But he was not a powerful trumpet player.
And I think that Lips and he copied each other. Well. Of course I never copied Lips.
